manifest.name: dsh-context-reclaim
manifest.description: DSH plugin: context reclaim at tool-result creation time, and at every later seam where context grows. Lossless noise purification, per-content-type bounding with retrieval pointers, tool-definition folding, system-prompt section-order stabilisation, and prompt-line trimming. Five Cordis seams, zero runtime dependencies. Also takes over the host's writable-request path, so the official `dsh-llm` file patch is no longer needed, and reports — without ever applying — which other official file patches are present. Never rewrites committed history, so the provider prefix cache is never invalidated.

bundle.text:
# dsh-context-reclaim — bundle patch
#
# 在官方 tools/post-execute 瀑布上做**创建时**的处理（那时消息还没进历史
# ⇒ 表面仍纯追加 ⇒ 不打断前缀缓存）。本插件**绝不改写已提交的历史**。
#
# 0.2.0 新增「按内容类型有界 + 取回指针」：
#   实测 117 个会话 / 36,458 条工具结果 / 57.08 MB：
#     sideEffect（pwsh 等）       28.41 -> 22.86 MB  省 5.55 MB（19.5%）
#     readOnly（read/grep/glob）  22.75 -> 16.81 MB  省 5.95 MB（26.1%）
#     faithful（web_fetch 等）    **一个字节不动**
#     合计                        57.08 -> 45.58 MB  省 11.50 MB（**20.1%**）
#
# 所有阈值都抄 <工作区>\上下文治理\01-权威依据\完整方案-上下文治理.yaml
# 的 parameters 段（Reasonix prune.go 的 readOnlySnip / sideEffectingSnip），**不是自己拍的**。
#
# 想整体关掉：把 enabled 改成 false。
# 只关有界、保留无损噪声：把 bounded 改成 false。
# 环境变量也能关：DSH_RECLAIM_BOUNDED=0 / DSH_RECLAIM_NOISE=0 / DSH_RECLAIM_STRIP_LINES=1。
# 改完必须重启 DSH（host 侧插件只在启动时读）。
- insert:
    - id: reclaim
      name: dsh-context-reclaim
      config:
        # 总开关；false 时插件整体不注册（零副作用）。
        enabled: true
        # 无损噪声净化：ANSI 转义 / 行尾空白 / 连续空行 / 回车折帧。语义上不可能改变内容。
        noise: true
        # 按内容类型有界 + 取回指针（0.2.0 新增）。
        bounded: true
        # 有损项：丢弃含百分比的进度行 / git 对象计数行。默认 false（可能丢信息）。
        stripLines: false
        # 省 >5% 才动结果（yaml noOpGuardRatio，出处 dsh-argp）。
        # 切行是有损的，不值得为 5% 以下收益做一次表面换代。
        noOpGuardRatio: 0.05
        # 超过它就放手，让官方 dsh-spill-policy 去落盘（那边还有 locator 与取回指引）。
        maxInlineBytes: 50000
        # 源在磁盘：头 80 行 / 尾 12 行，字符上限 10000 / 2000（Reasonix readOnlySnip）。
        readOnly:
          headLines: 80
          tailLines: 12
          headChars: 10000
          tailChars: 2000
        # 可重跑：头 40 / 尾 40，字符上限 8000 / 8000（Reasonix sideEffectingSnip）。
        # 给得比 readOnly 宽，因为副作用命令的输出不一定能重放出同样的字节。
        sideEffect:
          headLines: 40
          tailLines: 40
          headChars: 8000
          tailChars: 8000

readme.text: <div align="center">

**Tool results are reclaimed before they enter history, so the prompt cache never goes cold.**

> ⚠️ **DSH 1.5 only** (`>=0.1.5-rc.2 <0.2.0`). Newer DSH releases will be supported in follow-up updates.

> 🟢 **Collision risk: very low.** It occupies **5 server-side seams and 0 client slots** — measured alongside the **19 same-track plugins** among the 44 installed here, with no conflict, and it takes **no `chain` slot** (the only kind that makes plugins displace each other). See [Compatibility](#compatibility). [](LICENSE) [](#compatibility) [](#compatibility) **English** · [简体中文](README.zh-CN.md) ---

A DSH session's context is not blown up by the conversation; it is blown up by **tool results**: a single `read` of several hundred lines, a single `pwsh` dumping a wall of logs, a system prompt repeated verbatim every turn. Once this content has entered the history, the only thing left is for the compactor to operate on it after the fact — and compaction has to rewrite already-committed history, which knocks out the whole server-side prefix cache and makes every compaction more expensive than the last.

`dsh-context-reclaim` moves to a different position: it handles them **before the tool result is appended to history**, and it never rewrites content that has already been committed. So the prefix cache is never invalidated because of this plugin.

It hooks into 5 seams:

| Seam | What it does | Default |
|---|---|---|
| `tools/post-execute` | Purify a tool result the moment it is produced + bound it by content type, inserting a retrieval pointer at the truncation point | on |
| `system-prompt/assemble` | Fold the tool definition surface, stabilize the order of prefix sections, truncate over-long description lines | on |
| `tools/pre-execute` | Duplicate-edit interception (a second identical edit to the same content of the same file is rejected outright) | on |
| `session/event` | Compaction-summary integrity audit (warns when a compaction summary is missing sections) | on |
| `llm/stream` | One cost-attribution line per request, printing route / prompt / cache hit / output | on |
This is the core. Every time a tool call returns, the plugin first performs **lossless purification**, then **bounding**.

Collapses ANSI escape sequences, strips trailing whitespace, normalizes CR. This step is pure purification and loses no information.

It only acts when the content meets **both** thresholds: length ≥ 32 characters, and a reduction ratio after purification ≥ 0.2%. Small results are not touched at all.

Turn it off: `config.noise = false`, or the environment variable `DSH_RECLAIM_NOISE=0`.
Different types of tool results have completely different tolerances. The plugin sorts tools into three classes:

| Class | Tools covered | Head / tail kept | Per-line cap | Total character cap |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **Read-only** | `read` `grep` `glob` `codegraph_*` `lsp_*` | 80 lines / 12 lines | 512 | 160 |
| **Side-effecting** | `pwsh` `bash` `docker_*` `job_output` | 40 lines / 40 lines | 1024 | 256 |
| **Faithful** | `web_fetch` `web_search` `knowledge_*` `read_image` `pilot_snapshot` | left exactly as-is | — | — |

Tools it does not recognize are treated as **faithful** — better to save nothing than to cause unintended damage.

Wherever content was truncated, a retrieval pointer is inserted telling you how much of the original is left and how it can be retrieved, rather than dropping it silently.

The trigger threshold for bounding is "saves more than 5%"; if it does not save much, nothing is touched.

Turn it off: `config.bounded = false`, or the environment variable `DSH_RECLAIM_BOUNDED=0`.

> **About oversized results**: content above `config.maxInlineBytes` (default 50000) is handed to the spill mechanism to be written to disk. This requires the spill plugin to be installed in your profile — without it, this threshold has no effect and over-limit content passes through unchanged.

The lists for all three tool classes can be replaced wholesale in the configuration:

```yaml
- id: reclaim
  config:
    readOnlyTools: ['read', 'grep', 'glob']      # a full-table replacement, not an append
    sideEffectTools: ['pwsh', 'bash']

Note that this is a **full-table replacement**, not a per-field merge — writing only `headLines` will lose the character caps. Either write the whole table or write none of it.

---

At the start of every session, DSH stuffs the complete definitions (name, description, parameter schema) of every available tool into the system prompt. With dozens of plugins installed, this block can account for a large proportion of it, while most of those tools will not be used at all in the current turn.

By default the plugin **folds** this part: it keeps the full definitions of the most frequently used tools and compresses the rest into a one-line list (name + one-line description, no parameter schema).

**A folded tool is still callable.** The one-line list only removes the schema from the prompt — the tool itself stays registered with the host, so the model can still find it with `search_tools`, call it straight away with `invoke_tool`, or make it resident again with `load_plugin`. There is no `load_tools` tool; `search_tools` + `invoke_tool` is the pair. If you would rather keep every schema in the prompt, turn the folding off (next line).

Turn it off: `config.foldTools = false`, or the environment variable `DSH_RECLAIM_TOOL_FOLD=0`.

---

A server-side prefix cache only hits when the **prefix is byte-for-byte unchanged**. Yet the system prompt inherently carries a pile of things that change every turn: token counts, timestamps, session sequence numbers.

By default the plugin flattens these volatile numbers and reorders the sections so that stable sections come first and volatile ones last. Each reorder prints one `[reclaim/section-order]` line in the log, telling you which sections were moved.

---

The system prompt occasionally contains a single exceptionally long description line (long comments written by some plugins). Lines above the threshold (not exposed in `config`; the environment variable `DSH_RECLAIM_PROMPT_LINE_MAX`, default 120 characters) are truncated, and the line numbers that were truncated are printed to the log.

---

If the model issues exactly the same modification to the same content of the same file twice in a row, the second one is intercepted and an explanation is returned — such a call is almost certainly a meaningless duplicate that burns a whole round trip for nothing.

Log line: `[reclaim/dedup-deny]`.

Turn it off: the environment variable `DSH_RECLAIM_DEDUP_DENY=0`.

---

If the summary produced by the compactor is truncated by the output budget, it **silently** becomes shorter — you receive no notice at all, the next turn simply starts with a piece of the context missing.

After every compaction the plugin audits whether the summary contains the structural sections it should have, and warns when any are missing:

```
[reclaim/summary-audit] ⚠️ 摘要缺 3/8 段
```

It **only warns, it does not modify the summary**. What actually prevents summaries from being truncated is [`dsh-aux-degrade`](#-with-dsh-aux-degrade-the-context-governance-pair--install-both-together); see the interaction section below.

---

One line is printed at the end of every request:

```
[reclaim/usage] route=aux prompt=12043 hit=11890 miss=153 out=204 purpose=compaction
```

`hit` / `miss` are the prefix-cache hit and miss character counts, and `purpose` is the purpose of this call (if it has one). When the cache is broken, an extra `[reclaim/cache-break]` line is printed.

This log is the fastest entry point for diagnosing "why is my cache hit rate not high?".

---

The waterfall's `next` is a closure that **ignores its argument** and the adapter reads the outer `options`. So a plugin listening on `llm/stream` can *read* the request but cannot rewrite it — writing to a frozen object throws, and passing a new object to `next(...)` does nothing at all. That is why the desktop build of DSH has always shipped with a **local file patch** to `dsh-llm/lib/index.js` whose entire body is six lines: copy the frozen request shallowly, copy the messages array, re-mark it with `markAgentLoopRequest`, and hand the copy to the waterfall.
**Version 1.1.0 does the same thing from the plugin layer.** On load, this plugin wraps `ctx.llm.streamWithRegistration` once:

Because of this, **an unpatched install gets a writable request without a single file being touched.** Measured A/B on a stock runtime that carries no patches at all (`dsh --profile headless`, real request, `[reclaim/wire]` line):

```
[reclaim/wire] 入口探测：messages=5 条 · options 冻结=false · messages 冻结=false · route=deepseek-official|deepseek-flash|main|ba8a6419

[reclaim/wire] 入口探测：messages=5 条 · options 冻结=true  · messages 冻结=true  · route=deepseek-official|deepseek-flash|main|d7d22e75
```

Turn it off with `DSH_RECLAIM_WRITABLE_REQUEST=0`. The startup log tells you exactly what happened:

```
[reclaim/writable] 已接管 llm.streamWithRegistration：冻结的主请求先浅拷贝再进 llm/stream ⇒ 不再需要给官方 dsh-llm 打文件补丁（可用 dsh-llm 副本 2 份）
```

readme.section: The startup patch check — it reports, it never patches
readme.text:
On load the plugin inspects the official patch targets it can locate and prints exactly one line:

```
[reclaim/patch-check] 官方补丁体检（只读，本插件不会自动改官方文件）：7 个目标里未检测到 7 条 —— dsh-llm 可写请求、agent-loop 快照回收 / 系统提示收敛、…
```

readme.section: The startup patch check — it reports, it never patches
readme.text: It is deliberately **read-only**. This plugin is not a patcher: modifying files inside your DSH installation is your decision, not a side effect of installing a plugin. The check is a heuristic (it looks for the `*.orig` backups a patch script leaves next to the file it touched), so it says "not detected" rather than "not patched", and it stays completely silent when it cannot work out your install layout. Silence it with `DSH_RECLAIM_PATCH_CHECK=0`.

readme.section: The startup patch check — it reports, it never patches
readme.text: When something is missing and you do want it, do not hunt for a script — **hand the job to your own agent.** The file shipped inside this package, `tutorial-install-and-official-patches.md` (Chinese original: `tutorial-install-and-official-patches.zh-CN.md`), contains a ready-to-paste prompt describing each patch, its target, and its acceptance check; your agent reads it and patches your machine. That is the recommended route, because your agent can see your actual installation while a hard-coded script inside a plugin cannot.

9. The official-patch notice: one dialog, naming the patch and how to apply it
readme.text: The same dialog also lists **the other official patches** (owned by no plugin — apply them by symptom), so nothing goes unseen.

The configuration file is the profile's `cordis.patch.yml`:

```yaml
- id: reclaim
  config:
    enabled: true
    noise: true

| Key | Type | Default | Effect |
|---|---|---|---|
| `enabled` | boolean | `true` | Master switch (`!== false` counts as on) |
| `noise` | boolean | `true` | Lossless purification (ANSI / trailing whitespace / CR) |
| `bounded` | boolean | `true` | Bounding by content type + retrieval pointer |
| `stripLines` | boolean | `false` | Strip line-number prefixes |
| `noOpGuardRatio` | number | `0.05` | The "only act if it saves enough" threshold for bounding, 5% |
| `maxInlineBytes` | number | `50000` | Above this byte count, content goes to spill (spill plugin required) |
| `readOnlyTools` | string[] | see the table above | Read-only tool list, **a full-table replacement** |
| `sideEffectTools` | string[] | see the table above | Side-effecting tool list, **a full-table replacement** |
| `faithfulTools` | string[] | see the table above | Faithful tool list, **a full-table replacement** |
| `attribution` | boolean | `true` | Print the `[reclaim/usage]` attribution line |
| `trimSections` | boolean | `false` | Section trimming (note: the real gate is the environment variable `DSH_RECLAIM_SECTION_TRIM`, see below) |
| `foldTools` | boolean | `true` | Fold the tool definition surface |
| `

> ⚠️ The value of the `trimSections` option does not actually open the gate — the gate in the code only honours the environment variable `DSH_RECLAIM_SECTION_TRIM`, and it additionally requires `activePlugins` to be non-empty. The old documentation got this one wrong; it is stated accurately here.
There are more than 40 environment variables in total, covering every internal threshold. Grouped by function, the most commonly used ones are:

| Variable | Default | Effect |
|---|---|---|
| `DSH_RECLAIM_NOISE` | `1` | Set to `0` to turn off lossless purification |
| `DSH_RECLAIM_BOUNDED` | `1` | Set to `0` to turn off bounding |
| `DSH_RECLAIM_STRIP_LINES` | `0` | Set to `1` to strip line numbers |
| `DSH_RECLAIM_TOOL_FOLD` | `1` | Set to `0` to turn off tool definition surface folding |
| `DSH_RECLAIM_PROMPT_LINE_MAX` | `120` | Truncation threshold for a single system-prompt line |
| `DSH_RECLAIM_DEDUP_DENY` | `1` | Set to `0` to turn off duplicate-edit interception |
| `DSH_RECLAIM_SECTION_TRIM` | `0` | Set to `1` to turn on section trimming (works together with `activePlugins`) |
| `DSH_RECLAIM_STABILIZE` | `1` | Set to `0` to turn off prefix stabilization |
| `DSH_RECLAIM_WRITABLE_REQUEST` | `1` | Set to `0` to stop taking over `llm.streamWithRegistration` (see section 8); the official `dsh-llm` patch is only needed if you turn this off |
| `DSH_RECLAIM_PATCH_CHECK` | `1` | Set to `0` to silence the one-line "official patch check" notice printed at startup |
| `DSH_RECLAIM_LOG` | `1` | Set to `0` to turn off this plugin's log output |
| `DSH_RECLAIM_DUMP_SYSTEM` | `0` | Set to `1` to dump the assembled system prompt

The remaining threshold variables (sampling line counts, budget observation, pollution-detection window, archive limits, reasoning stripping, etc.) each have a per-item comment at the top of the source.

readme.section: Coexistence: does it fight other plugins? (measured 2026-10-15)
readme.text:
**This plugin hooks five server-side seams**: `llm/stream`, `tools/pre-execute`, `tools/post-execute`, `system-prompt/assemble`, `session/event` — more than any of the other three.

Of the 44 plugins installed on the test machine, **19** share at least one seam with it, and 18 of those are **cooperative** (every handler calls `next()` to pass through). It runs alongside all of them, including `dsh-vision-router`, which shares three seams — **measured, no conflict**.

readme.section: Coexistence: does it fight other plugins? (measured 2026-10-15)
readme.text:
The reason: DSH event seams are a **middleware waterfall**. As long as every party calls `next()` and only makes incremental edits, they **compose** rather than pre-empt.

**Client slots**: this plugin occupies **none** — it is a server-side plugin with no front end.

readme.section: 💡 Companion advice: add a context-compression plugin (not part of this project)
readme.text: What this plugin does is keep **the request from growing without bound and the prefix from moving**: tool-result purification, bounding by content type, tool-definition folding, description-line truncation, duplicate-edit interception, summary-integrity audit, cost attribution, and making the request *writable* (section 8).

readme.section: 💡 Companion advice: add a context-compression plugin (not part of this project)
readme.text:
What it does **not** do is turn a long history into a summary. So we recommend installing a **context-compression / history-summarisation** plugin as well — they are complementary: the compression plugin collapses history as the conversation grows, while this plugin keeps the prefix stable across that compression and keeps the raw material (tool results) from inflating. A stable prefix is easier to cache-hit, which is cheaper.

> **⚠️ These numbers are the best case under a long continuous run — not the normal case, not promises, not limits and not a quote.**
> In practice many things keep you from reaching them: a broken prefix (switching models mid-session, a changed system prompt, reordered context, another plugin inserting new content near the front); material that keeps arriving (a new skill catalogue, new MCP tools, very long documents, pasting large blocks); compression happening at a bad moment or tool results inflating beyond expectation; switching tasks, opening fresh sessions often, a changing tool surface; changed model pricing, cache policy or provider. **Real behaviour on your machine is what counts.**

A compression plugin from anyone else works too.

readme.section: 🔗 With `dsh-aux-degrade` (the context governance pair) — install both together
readme.text:
`dsh-context-reclaim` and [`dsh-aux-degrade`](https://github.com/xiamubumu/dsh-aux-degrade) are the two halves of the same "context governance" scheme. **Installing both together is strongly recommended; this is the most important interaction this plugin has.**

**① They share the same routing criterion.** Both plugins use the same test to tell a "main-conversation call" from an "auxiliary call":

```
tools.length > 0 ? 'main' : 'aux'
```

readme.section: 🔗 With `dsh-aux-degrade` (the context governance pair) — install both together
readme.text: reclaim uses it to tag cost attribution with `route=`, and aux-degrade uses it to decide whether to lower the reasoning effort of this call. **The criterion must be identical**, otherwise the two plugins will disagree about "which call counts as an auxiliary call", one saving while the other leaks.

readme.section: 🔗 With `dsh-aux-degrade` (the context governance pair) — install both together
readme.text:
**② How they divide the work.** reclaim handles **content** (purification and bounding of tool results before they enter history, tool definition surface folding, prefix stabilization); aux-degrade handles **calls** (lowering the reasoning effort of auxiliary calls such as compaction summaries / session titles to `off`, and appending two faithful-preservation requirements to the compaction instruction).

**③ What happens without the other.**

readme.section: 🔗 With `dsh-aux-degrade` (the context governance pair) — install both together
readme.text:
| Installed alone | Result |
|---|---|
| Only reclaim | Everything works as usual. But auxiliary calls still burn the full reasoning budget, and compaction summaries can still be truncated by the output cap — reclaim will only print `[reclaim/summary-audit] ⚠️ 摘要缺 N/8 段` in the log to remind you, **it will not modify the summary itself** (this is deliberate: reclaim does not touch committed content) |
| Only aux-degrade | Everything works as usual. But tool results are not purified or bounded, and long results enter history unchanged |

readme.section: 🔗 With `dsh-aux-degrade` (the context governance pair) — install both together
readme.text: **④ They do not depend on each other.** reclaim's source contains **no `import` / `require` at all**, and aux-degrade only imports the official `@deepseek-ai/schemastery`. They do not probe each other and do not reference each other — **either one can be installed alone and work normally**, just with different coverage. This is also why they are two repositories rather than one.

readme.section: 🔗 With `dsh-aux-degrade` (the context governance pair) — install both together
readme.text: **⑤ One practical detail.** If you turn on reclaim's `[reclaim/usage]` attribution log, you will see a `purpose=` field in it. That field exists to diagnose "**which class of auxiliary call is not being lowered to off by aux-degrade**" — it is a read-only diagnostic that changes no behaviour. When you see `purpose=unknown` or a purpose you have never seen before, that usually means some auxiliary call path bypasses the degrade criterion.

readme.section: 🔗 With `dsh-aux-degrade` (the context governance pair) — install both together
readme.text: **⑥ In one sentence.** With reclaim installed and aux-degrade missing, you will see the problem but cannot fix it; with aux-degrade installed and reclaim missing, your auxiliary calls are saved but your tool results are not. Install both, and context governance is complete.

reclaim internally maintains an ownership table of "which section of the system prompt belongs to whom" (`SECTION_OWNER`), in which the "available plugins" section belongs to [`dsh-capability-composer`](https://github.com/xiamubumu/dsh-capability-composer).

In other words: **the plugin list should not be trimmed by reclaim** — that is the capability composer's job. When both are installed, narrowing of the section is carried out by the composer, and reclaim only keeps the default behaviour when the composer is absent.

No direct coupling. The two can be installed in any combination.

---

Will it break my prefix cache? No. This is the most important design constraint of the plugin: **it only acts before content enters history, and never rewrites content that has already been committed**. The committed part stays byte-for-byte identical, so the prefix cache will never be invalidated because of reclaim.
Will it alter my tool output?

It only truncates when the threshold is exceeded, and it always leaves a retrieval pointer at the truncation point. The purification layer is lossless (ANSI escapes, trailing whitespace — things that carry no information in the first place). In addition, three classes of tools are listed as "faithful": **they pass through unchanged, not a single character is touched**.
Do I need to restart after installing?

Yes. Host-side plugins are loaded when DSH starts. After one restart it stays in effect.
Will it install anything else into my profile? No. The plugin has zero runtime dependencies, `peerDependencies` declares only official packages, and the installation process introduces no third-party code.
How do I know how much it actually saved?

Look at the `hit` / `miss` fields of the `[reclaim/usage]` log line — those are the real per-request prefix-cache character counts. A truncated result carries its own note at the truncation point (how much was saved, how to retrieve it).
Does it support web DSH?

Yes. This plugin is a host-side plugin and only depends on Cordis's generic seams (`tools/post-execute`, `system-prompt/assemble`, `session/event`, `llm/stream`), with no dependency on Electron or any desktop-only capability. **As long as it is DSH, both desktop and web work.**
Why are there two plugins both called "context governance"?

Because they handle two different layers of the same thing: one handles **content** (how results are processed before entering history), the other handles **calls** (how much reasoning budget an auxiliary call spends). See the [interaction section](#-with-dsh-aux-degrade-the-context-governance-pair--install-both-together) above.
</details>

DSH 会话的上下文不是被对话撑爆的，是被**工具结果**撑爆的：一次 `read` 几百行、一次 `pwsh` 一大片日志、一份系统提示每轮原样重复。这些内容一旦进了历史，就只能靠压缩器事后动刀——而压缩要重写已提交的历史，会把服务端前缀缓存整段打掉，越压越贵。

`dsh-context-reclaim` 换了个位置：**在工具结果被 append 进历史之前**就处理掉，并且从不改写已经提交的内容。所以前缀缓存永远不会因为本插件而失效。

它挂在 5 个接缝上：

| 接缝 | 做什么 | 默认 |
|---|---|---|
| `tools/post-execute` | 工具结果一产生就净化 + 按内容类型有界化，截断处插入取回指针 | 开 |
| `system-prompt/assemble` | 折叠工具定义面、稳定前缀段顺序、截断超长描述行 | 开 |
| `tools/pre-execute` | 重复编辑拦截（同一个文件同一段内容改第二次直接拦下） | 开 |
| `session/event` | 摘要完整性审计（压缩摘要缺段时报警） | 开 |
| `llm/stream` | 每请求一行成本归因，打出 route / prompt / 缓存命中 / 输出 | 开 |

readme.section: 1. 工具结果净化与有界化
readme.text: 这是核心。每次工具调用返回时，插件先做**无损净化**，再做**有界化**。

折叠 ANSI 转义序列、去掉行尾空白、统一 CR。这一步是纯净化，不丢任何信息。

只有在内容**同时**满足两个门槛时才动手：长度 ≥ 32 字符，且净化后缩减比例 ≥ 0.2%。小结果根本不碰。

关掉它：`config.noise = false` 或环境变量 `DSH_RECLAIM_NOISE=0`。

不同类型的工具结果，容忍度完全不同。插件把工具分成三类：

| 类别 | 覆盖的工具 | 头 / 尾保留 | 单行上限 | 总字符上限 |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **只读** | `read` `grep` `glob` `codegraph_*` `lsp_*` | 80 行 / 12 行 | 512 | 160 |
| **有副作用** | `pwsh` `bash` `docker_*` `job_output` | 40 行 / 40 行 | 1024 | 256 |
| **保真** | `web_fetch` `web_search` `knowledge_*` `read_image` `pilot_snapshot` | 原样不动 | — | — |

认不出来的工具按**保真**处理——宁可不省，也不误伤。

被截断的地方会插入一个取回指针，告诉你原文还有多少、可以用什么方式取回，而不是无声无息地丢掉。

有界化的触发门槛是「能省下超过 5%」；省得不多就不动。

关掉它：`config.bounded = false` 或环境变量 `DSH_RECLAIM_BOUNDED=0`。

> **关于超大结果**：超过 `config.maxInlineBytes`（默认 50000）的内容会交给 spill 机制落盘。这需要你的 profile 里装了 spill 插件——没有装的话，这个阈值不生效，超限内容原样通过。

三类工具的名单都可以在配置里整表替换：

```yaml
- id: reclaim
  config:
    readOnlyTools: ['read', 'grep', 'glob']      # 整表替换，不是追加
    sideEffectTools: ['pwsh', 'bash']

注意这是**整表替换**，不是逐字段合并——只写 `headLines` 会丢掉字符上限。要么整张表写全，要么别写。

---

每个会话一开始，DSH 会把所有可用工具的完整定义（名字、描述、参数 schema）塞进系统提示。装了几十个插件之后，这一块能占到很大比例，而其中大部分工具在这一轮里根本不会被用到。

插件默认**折叠**这部分：保留最常用的若干个完整定义，其余压成一行清单（只有名字 + 一句话描述，没有参数 schema）。

**被折叠的工具照样能调。** 一行清单只是把 schema 从提示里拿掉了 —— 工具本身仍然注册在宿主上，所以模型依然可以用 `search_tools` 找到它、用 `invoke_tool` 直接调用，或用 `load_plugin` 让它重新常驻。**没有 `load_tools` 这个工具**，配对的是 `search_tools` + `invoke_tool`。如果你更希望每个 schema 都留在提示里，就关掉折叠（见下一行）。

关掉它：`config.foldTools = false` 或环境变量 `DSH_RECLAIM_TOOL_FOLD=0`。

---

服务端前缀缓存只在**前缀逐字节不变**时才命中。而系统提示里天生带一堆每轮都在变的东西：token 计数、时间戳、会话序号。

插件默认抹平这些易变数字，并重排段落顺序让稳定的段排在前面、易变的段排在后面。每次重排会在日志里打一行 `[reclaim/section-order]`，告诉你哪几段被移动了。

---

系统提示里偶尔会有单行特别长的描述（某些插件写的长注释）。超过阈值（`config` 里没有暴露，环境变量 `DSH_RECLAIM_PROMPT_LINE_MAX`，默认 120 字符）的行会被截断，并在日志打出被截断的行号。

---

同一个文件、同一段内容，如果模型连续两次发起完全一样的修改，第二次会被拦下并返回说明——这种调用几乎必然是无意义的重复，白白烧一次往返。

日志行：`[reclaim/dedup-deny]`。

关掉它：环境变量 `DSH_RECLAIM_DEDUP_DENY=0`。

---

压缩器生成的摘要如果被输出预算截断，会**静默**变短——你不会收到任何提示，只是下一轮开始上下文就缺了一块。

插件在每次压缩后审计摘要是否包含应有的结构段，缺了就报警：

```
[reclaim/summary-audit] ⚠️ 摘要缺 3/8 段
```

它**只报警，不改摘要**。真正防止摘要被截断的是 [`dsh-aux-degrade`](#-与-dsh-aux-degrade上下文治理两件套--请务必一起安装)，见下面的联动章节。

---

每个请求结束打一行：

```
[reclaim/usage] route=aux prompt=12043 hit=11890 miss=153 out=204 purpose=compaction
```

`hit` / `miss` 是前缀缓存的命中与未命中字符数，`purpose` 是这次调用的用途（如果有）。缓存被打破时会另外打一行 `[reclaim/cache-break]`。

这个日志是排查「为什么我的缓存命中率不高」最快的入口。

---

readme.section: 8. 接管「可写请求」——不需要给 `dsh-llm` 打补丁
8. 接管「可写请求」——不需要给 `dsh-llm` 打补丁
readme.text:
瀑布的 `next` 是**忽略参数**的闭包，适配器读的是外层那个 `options`。所以挂在 `llm/stream` 上的插件只能**看**这个请求，改不了它——往冻结对象上写会抛错，把新对象传给 `next(...)` 则完全没有效果。桌面版 DSH 一直随包带一个 **`dsh-llm/lib/index.js` 的文件补丁**，全部内容就六行：把冻结请求浅拷贝一份、连 `messages` 数组一起拷、用 `markAgentLoopRequest` 重新打标记，再把副本交给瀑布。

**1.0.0 起，本插件在插件层做了同一件事。** 它在加载时把 `ctx.llm.streamWithRegistration` 包一层：

readme.section: 8. 接管「可写请求」——不需要给 `dsh-llm` 打补丁
readme.text:
* 请求**冻结** → 浅拷贝 + 拷 `messages` 数组 + 逐个拷消息对象，再用**宿主自己那份** `dsh-llm` 模块里的 `markAgentLoopRequest` 重新打标记，副本才进 `llm/stream`；
* 请求**没冻结**（宿主已经打过补丁）→ 原样透传，逐字节不变，行为零变化；
* 出现任何意外 → 记一条日志后原样透传。本插件绝不会把一个能用的会话弄坏。

因此，**一个补丁都没打的原版运行环境，不碰任何文件就能拿到可写请求。** 在一个完全零补丁的真实运行时上（`dsh --profile headless`，真实请求，`[reclaim/wire]` 行）实测 A/B：

```
[reclaim/wire] 入口探测：messages=5 条 · options 冻结=false · messages 冻结=false · route=deepseek-official|deepseek-flash|main|ba8a6419

[reclaim/wire] 入口探测：messages=5 条 · options 冻结=true  · messages 冻结=true  · route=deepseek-official|deepseek-flash|main|d7d22e75
```

用 `DSH_RECLAIM_WRITABLE_REQUEST=0` 可以关掉它。启动日志会把实际情况说清楚：

```
[reclaim/writable] 已接管 llm.streamWithRegistration：冻结的主请求先浅拷贝再进 llm/stream ⇒ 不再需要给官方 dsh-llm 打文件补丁（可用 dsh-llm 副本 2 份）
```

readme.section: 它怎么找到「宿主自己那一份」模块
readme.text: `markAgentLoopRequest` 往一个 `WeakSet` 里写，而这个集合**只存在于某一个模块实例内部**；Node 对每一个不同的模块 URL 都会造一份独立实例。用别的实例去标记等于白标：别的插件在那个集合里查不到你的对象。所以本插件：

readme.section: 它怎么找到「宿主自己那一份」模块
readme.text:
1. 从 `process.argv` 推导候选位置（真正的 `…/@deepseek-ai/dsh/lib/bin.js`——桌面外壳里它在 `argv[2]`，不是 `argv[1]`），再用 `createRequire` 从宿主入口解析一次，再补上 `$DSH_HOME/profiles{/*}/node_modules` 这两条软链接拼法；
2. 逐个 import，并对着**当前这个真实请求**做**往返自检**：第一个 `isAgentLoopRequest(options)` 返回 `true` 的，就是宿主自己那份，用它；
3. 一个都不匹配时，打一次警告，然后仍然用第一份接管。**这条限制如实说：** 这种情况下上下文改写照常生效，但 `@deepseek-ai/dsh-session-title` 可能不再自动给会话起标题，因为它查的是同一个 `WeakSet`。该现象在某种 npm 安装布局上出现过，桌面端布局上没有。DSH 内部除它之外没有别的消费者。

readme.section: 它怎么找到「宿主自己那一份」模块
readme.text: 如果检测到 `invariants` 服务存在（`dsh-agent-loop` 的「循环请求必须冻结」断言），本插件会自动**跳过接管**——否则会话会被断言中断。现有 1.5 的任何 profile 都没有加载它，但真出现了我们宁可让路，也不弄断你的会话。

readme.section: 启动时的「官方补丁体检」——只报告，绝不动手
readme.text:
插件加载时会扫一遍它能定位到的官方补丁目标，然后打**且只打一行**：

```
[reclaim/patch-check] 官方补丁体检（只读，本插件不会自动改官方文件）：7 个目标里未检测到 7 条 —— dsh-llm 可写请求、agent-loop 快照回收 / 系统提示收敛、…
```

它刻意做成**只读**。本插件不是补丁器：改动你 DSH 安装目录里的文件，是你的决定，不该是「装了个插件」的副作用。判据是启发式（找补丁脚本在文件旁边留下的 `*.orig` 备份），所以说的是「未检测到」而不是「没打」；一旦推导不出你的安装布局，它就完全闭嘴。用 `DSH_RECLAIM_PATCH_CHECK=0` 可以关掉。

readme.section: 启动时的「官方补丁体检」——只报告，绝不动手
readme.text:
真有想打又没打上的，别去找脚本——**把这件事交给你的 agent。** 本插件包里的 `tutorial-install-and-official-patches.zh-CN.md`（英文版 `tutorial-install-and-official-patches.md`）有一段可以直接整段复制的提示词，写清了每条补丁改哪个文件、验收标准是什么；你的 agent 读完就在你自己的机器上打。**推荐走这条路**，因为你的 agent 看得到你真实的安装目录，而写在插件里的硬编码脚本看不到。

> **补丁库：官方 10 条补丁已单独开源 → <https://github.com/xiamubumu/dsh-patch-library>** 补丁本体、自适应应用器、五种打法、一键回退都在里面。`node apply.mjs --check` 是只读体检，`--apply` 自动备份并逐个 `node --check`，`--revert` 一键还原。

readme.section: 其余官方补丁：插件能替代什么、不能替代什么
readme.text:

readme.section: 9. 官方补丁提醒：装好就弹一次，指到哪条、怎么打
readme.text:
- **哪条补丁**：列出补丁 id、改哪个包的哪个文件、以及本插件为什么需要它（写清楚「必须」还是「建议」）；
- **怎么打（三种，任选一种）**：**A** 点弹窗里的「复制提示词」，把整段发给**你自己的 agent**（它先跑只读体检、再逐条打、hunk 对不上就停下问你）；**B** 用补丁库的脚本 `node apply.mjs --check` / `node apply.mjs --apply --only <id>`；**C** 手动 `cd <被改包> && git apply -p1 <库>/patches/<id>/change.diff`；
- **补丁库**：<https://github.com/xiamubumu/dsh-patch-library>（10 条自包含补丁 + 自适应应用器 + 五种打法）；
- **检测系统**：按目标文件旁的 `*.orig` 备份 + **内容哈希**（对补丁库清单里的 `pristine` / `patched`）判断打没打；两者都不确定时它**明说「无法判定」**，绝不猜「已打」；
- **打完就不再弹**。弹窗里可以「稍后再说」（只关这一次）或「不再提醒」（永久，且**按补丁 id 记** —— 将来新增的补丁仍然会提醒你）。

readme.section: 9. 官方补丁提醒：装好就弹一次，指到哪条、怎么打
readme.text: 同一个弹窗还会列出**其余官方补丁**（不绑定本插件，按你遇到的症状决定打不打），保证一条都不漏。

配置文件是 profile 的 `cordis.patch.yml`：

```yaml
- id: reclaim
  config:
    enabled: true
    noise: true

| 键 | 类型 | 默认 | 作用 |
|---|---|---|---|
| `enabled` | boolean | `true` | 总开关（`!== false` 即视为开） |
| `noise` | boolean | `true` | 无损净化（ANSI / 行尾空白 / CR） |
| `bounded` | boolean | `true` | 按内容类型有界化 + 取回指针 |
| `stripLines` | boolean | `false` | 剥离行号前缀 |
| `noOpGuardRatio` | number | `0.05` | 有界化「省得够多才动手」的门槛，5% |
| `maxInlineBytes` | number | `50000` | 超过这个字节数交给 spill（需装 spill 插件） |
| `readOnlyTools` | string[] | 见上表 | 只读类工具名单，**整表替换** |
| `sideEffectTools` | string[] | 见上表 | 有副作用类工具名单，**整表替换** |
| `faithfulTools` | string[] | 见上表 | 保真类工具名单，**整表替换** |
| `attribution` | boolean | `true` | 打 `[reclaim/usage]` 归因行 |
| `trimSections` | boolean | `false` | 段落收纳（注意：实际闸门是环境变量 `DSH_RECLAIM_SECTION_TRIM`，见下） |
| `foldTools` | boolean | `true` | 折叠工具定义面 |
| `activePlugins` | string[] | `[]` | 参与段归属计算的插件名单 |
> ⚠️ `trimSections` 这个配置项的取值不会真正开门——代码里的闸门只认环境变量 `DSH_RECLAIM_SECTION_TRIM`，而且还需要 `activePlugins` 非空。这一条在旧文档里说法有误，这里如实写出。

| 变量 | 默认 | 作用 |
|---|---|---|
| `DSH_RECLAIM_NOISE` | `1` | 设 `0` 关无损净化 |
| `DSH_RECLAIM_BOUNDED` | `1` | 设 `0` 关有界化 |
| `DSH_RECLAIM_STRIP_LINES` | `0` | 设 `1` 剥离行号 |
| `DSH_RECLAIM_TOOL_FOLD` | `1` | 设 `0` 关工具定义面折叠 |
| `DSH_RECLAIM_PROMPT_LINE_MAX` | `120` | 系统提示单行截断阈值 |
| `DSH_RECLAIM_DEDUP_DENY` | `1` | 设 `0` 关重复编辑拦截 |
| `DSH_RECLAIM_SECTION_TRIM` | `0` | 设 `1` 开段落收纳（配合 `activePlugins`） |
| `DSH_RECLAIM_STABILIZE` | `1` | 设 `0` 关前缀稳定化 |
| `DSH_RECLAIM_WRITABLE_REQUEST` | `1` | 设 `0` 停止接管 `llm.streamWithRegistration`（见第 8 节）；关掉它之后才需要官方 `dsh-llm` 补丁 |
| `DSH_RECLAIM_PATCH_CHECK` | `1` | 设 `0` 关闭启动时那行「官方补丁体检」提示 |
| `DSH_RECLAIM_LOG` | `1` | 设 `0` 关本插件的日志输出 |
| `DSH_RECLAIM_DUMP_SYSTEM` | `0` | 设 `1` 把组装好的系统提示转储到临时目录，用于排查 |

其余阈值类变量（采样行数、预算观测、污染检测窗口、归档上限、推理剥离等）在源码顶部有逐条注释。

readme.section: 共存实测：会不会和别的插件打架（2026-10-15 实测）
readme.text:
**本插件挂了 5 个服务端接缝**：`llm/stream`、`tools/pre-execute`、`tools/post-execute`、`system-prompt/assemble`、`session/event` —— 是四个自研插件里最多的一个。

本机 44 个已装插件里，**19 个**与本插件共享至少一个接缝，其中 18 个是**协作式**的（每个 handler 都调用 `next()` 往下传）。本插件与它们**同机共存**，包括共享 3 个接缝的 `dsh-vision-router` —— **实测无冲突**。

原因：DSH 的事件接缝是**中间件瀑布**。只要各方都调 `next()`、只做增量修改，就是**叠加**而不是抢占。

**客户端槽位**：本插件**一个都不占** —— 它是纯服务端插件，没有前端。

**已知会撞的三种情况（如实）**

readme.section: 共存实测：会不会和别的插件打架（2026-10-15 实测）
readme.text:
1. 对方在**同一个服务端接缝**上做**整体重建**（把 system prompt / 工具结果整个重写），而不是增量修改；
2. 对方占用**同一个 `chain` 型**槽位（本插件不占任何槽位，所以只有对方受这条影响）；
3. 双方要求打**同一个官方文件**的补丁 —— 这一条会被补丁库的 `apply.mjs --check` **明确报 `conflict`**，不会静默出错。

**已实测共存**：`dsh-context-reclaim` + `billion-context@0.1.175` 同机同 profile 无冲突 —— 前者走 **Cordis 事件总线**，后者走 **agent 引导层**（bootstrap-hook / native loader，自带 6 种 agent 的打包产物），两者**没有共享接缝**。

readme.section: 💡 搭配建议：再加一个「上下文压缩」插件（不是本项目的插件）
readme.text:
本插件负责的是「**别让请求越长越大、别让前缀抖动**」：工具结果净化、按类型有界化、工具定义面折叠、描述行截断、重复编辑拦截、摘要完整性审计、成本归因，以及把请求变成*可写*（第 8 节）。

它**不负责把长历史压成摘要**。所以推荐你再装一个**上下文压缩 / 历史摘要**类插件 —— 两者互补：压缩插件在对话变长时把历史收拢，本插件保证压缩前后前缀稳定、被压缩的原料（工具结果）本身不膨胀。前缀越稳，缓存越容易命中，也就越省钱。

**实测记录（本机，2026-10-14，仅供参考）**

| 指标 | 实测值 |
|---|---|
| 长会话上下文规模 | **涨不到 200K** |
| 前缀缓存命中 | 约 **98%** |
| 成本（**最佳情况**） | 约半小时 **不到 ¥3**（人民币，按当时的模型单价与用量；峰值，不是常态） |

readme.section: 💡 搭配建议：再加一个「上下文压缩」插件（不是本项目的插件）
readme.text:
> **⚠️ 这组数字是「长时间连续运行时」的最佳/峰值表现 —— 不是常态，不是承诺，不是上限，也不是报价。**
> 实际使用中很多情况会让它达不到：前缀被破坏（中途换模型 / 系统提示变化 / 上下文顺序改变 / 有插件往前面塞新内容）；有新内容持续加进来（新技能目录、新 MCP 工具、超长文档、频繁贴大段材料）；压缩时机不合适或工具结果超预期膨胀；单轮任务切换、频繁新开会话、工具面变化；模型单价、缓存策略或服务方变更。**一切以你机器上的真实运行为准。**

**搭配对象由你自己选。** 我们实测时用的那款是第三方插件 **`billion-context`** —— 它**不是本项目的插件**，与本项目**没有任何关联**（不是依赖、不是合作、不随本插件安装），这里只是如实记录「我们拿它一起跑过」。你要是用别家的压缩插件，同样可以配。

**本插件只为自己承诺**：前缀稳定化、工具结果有界化、压缩前的请求可写。压缩效果与最终成本由你实际使用的模型、缓存策略、对话内容决定。

---

readme.section: 🔗 与 `dsh-aux-degrade`（上下文治理两件套）—— 请务必一起安装
readme.text:
`dsh-context-reclaim` 与 [`dsh-aux-degrade`](https://github.com/xiamubumu/dsh-aux-degrade) 是同一套「上下文治理」方案的两半。**强烈建议同时安装，这是本插件最重要的联动关系。**

**① 它们共享同一个路由口径。** 两个插件都用同一个判据区分「主对话调用」与「辅助调用」：

```
tools.length > 0 ? 'main' : 'aux'
```

reclaim 用它给成本归因打 `route=` 标签，aux-degrade 用它决定要不要给这次调用降思考强度。**口径必须一致**，否则两个插件对「哪一次调用算辅助调用」的判断会打架，一边省着、一边漏着。

**② 它们的分工。** reclaim 管**内容**（工具结果进历史前的净化与有界化、工具定义面折叠、前缀稳定化）；aux-degrade 管**调用**（把压缩摘要 / 会话标题这类辅助调用的思考强度降到 `off`，并给压缩指令追加两节保真要求）。

**③ 缺了对方会怎样。**

readme.section: 🔗 与 `dsh-aux-degrade`（上下文治理两件套）—— 请务必一起安装
readme.text:
| 只装 | 结果 |
|---|---|
| 只有 reclaim | 一切照常工作。但辅助调用仍会烧满思考预算，压缩摘要仍可能被输出顶截断——reclaim 只会在日志里打 `[reclaim/summary-audit] ⚠️ 摘要缺 N/8 段` 提醒你，**它自己不会去改摘要**（这是有意的：reclaim 不碰已提交内容） |
| 只有 aux-degrade | 一切照常工作。但工具结果不会被净化与有界化，长结果原样进历史 |

**④ 两者互不依赖。** reclaim 源码里**没有任何 `import` / `require`**，aux-degrade 只 import 官方的 `@deepseek-ai/schemastery`。它们不互相探测、不互相引用——**任何一个都能单独安装并正常工作**，只是覆盖度不同。这也是为什么它们是两个仓库而不是一个。

readme.section: 🔗 与 `dsh-aux-degrade`（上下文治理两件套）—— 请务必一起安装
readme.text:
**⑤ 一个实用细节。** 如果你打开 reclaim 的 `[reclaim/usage]` 归因日志，会看到里面有个 `purpose=` 字段。这个字段就是用来诊断「**哪一类辅助调用没被 aux-degrade 降到 off**」的——它是一次只读诊断，不改任何行为。看到 `purpose=unknown` 或某个没见过的 purpose 时，那通常意味着有一条辅助调用路径绕过了降级判据。

**⑥ 一句话。** 装了 reclaim 不装 aux-degrade，你会看到问题但修不掉；装了 aux-degrade 不装 reclaim，你的辅助调用省了但工具结果没省。两个一起装，上下文治理才是完整的。

reclaim 内部维护一张「哪一段系统提示归谁管」的归属表（`SECTION_OWNER`），其中「可用插件」这一段归 [`dsh-capability-composer`](https://github.com/xiamubumu/dsh-capability-composer)。

也就是说：**装插件清单不该由 reclaim 来裁剪**——那是能力组合器的职责。两者同时安装时，段的收窄交给组合器执行，reclaim 只在组合器不在场时保留默认行为。

无直接耦合。两者可以任意组合安装。

---

它会破坏我的前缀缓存吗？ 不会。这是本插件最重要的一条设计约束：**它只在内容进入历史之前动手，从不改写已经提交的内容**。已提交部分逐字节不变，前缀缓存因此永远不会因为 reclaim 而失效。
它会把我的工具输出改掉吗？ 只在超过阈值时截断，并且一定在截断处留下取回指针。净化那一层是无损的（ANSI 转义、行尾空白这类本来就不携带信息的东西）。另外有三类工具被列为「保真」，**原样通过，一个字符都不动**。
装完要重启吗？ 要。宿主侧插件在 DSH 启动时装载。重启一次之后就一直生效。
它会往我的 profile 里装别的东西吗？

不会。本插件零运行时依赖，`peerDependencies` 只声明官方包，安装过程不会引入任何第三方代码。
我怎么知道它到底省了多少？ 看 `[reclaim/usage]` 日志行的 `hit` / `miss` 字段，那是每请求的真实前缀缓存字符数。被截断的结果会在截断处自带说明（省了多少、怎么取回）。
支持网页版 DSH 吗？ 支持。本插件是宿主侧插件，只依赖 Cordis 的通用接缝（`tools/post-execute`、`system-prompt/assemble`、`session/event`、`llm/stream`），不依赖任何 Electron 或桌面专属能力。**只要是 DSH，桌面版和网页版都能用。**
为什么有两个插件都叫「上下文治理」？

因为它们管的是两层不同的事：一个管**内容**（结果进历史前怎么处理），一个管**调用**（辅助调用花多少思考预算）。见上面的[联动章节](#-与-dsh-aux-degrade上下文治理两件套--请务必一起安装)。
</details>
